Exclusive Comet Unlocks
Auto-Ascend Ritual
Choose which Rift to defeat before automatic Ascension. Toggle it on or off anytime. Your chosen target persists across Ascensions.
Comet Trials
Unlock Quiet Guardian and Single Star run challenges. One Trial at a time, beginning after your next Ascend. Completing each earns a permanent cosmetic mark. No power or currency bonus; starts and retries are free.
Rift Trail
An optional starlight trail around the Rift. One trail slot, independent of your aura. Static with reduced motion. Cosmetic only.
Starfall Crest
An optional star emblem beside your Guardian and on Ascension. One crest slot, independent of your aura. Cosmetic only.
Cosmetics
Certain Deeds unlock a new aura for the Rift. Purely visual — never a power gain.

Settings

Fair Play
Our promise
No pay-to-win, ever
Lumenfall has nothing to buy with real money — every currency, from Lumen to Sigils, is earned by playing. Every upgrade you see is something you can reach yourself.
The "zone 80 wall"
Progress never fully stalls
Many idle RPGs stretch their upgrade paths thin enough that progress plateaus for days at a time. Every Ascend here guarantees Prisms the moment you qualify, and Rarity plus Rift Forge upgrades never get wiped — so a reset is always a net gain.
"Present every few minutes"
Actually idle
Some idle games expect hours of daily babysitting or you hit a hard stop. Your Wisps keep fighting while you’re away, with generous, transparent offline earnings shown the moment you return.
"24 heroes at once"
A roster that unfolds
Wisps unlock gradually as you go deeper, instead of dumping a full cast on a brand-new player.
Gear rarity RNG
No loot boxes, no gacha
Every upgrade — leveling, Rarity, Rift Forge upgrades — is a visible, deterministic purchase, and even a Luminous enemy always drops the same fixed amount of Motes. What you see is what you get, never a random range.
What actually makes an idle RPG feel like one
A real party, with real roles
Up to five Wisps — each with a class, a resource bar, and an active ability — fight beside your Guardian. Their Rarity tier and Forge investment matter, not just one flat number going up.
Real taps only
Autoclickers earn nothing extra
Manual tapping is capped to what a genuinely fast human can do, and only real touch or click input counts toward damage — a script mashing the Rift in the background gets no more than your Wisps were already earning on their own.
Save
This permanently deletes every Wisp, Rarity tier, Rift Forge upgrade, Research Project, Prism, Motes, Comet and Deed. This cannot be undone.

Currencies
Lumen
Earned from every kill. Spend it to recruit and empower Wisps, and to fund Rift Forge upgrades and Research Lab projects.
Shards
Also earned from every kill, in smaller amounts. Spend it to raise a Wisp’s Rarity tier and to fund Rift Forge upgrades and Research Lab projects.
Motes
Dropped only by rare Luminous enemies in the Rift, always a fixed amount. Spend it to speed up your active Research Project in the Research Lab.
Prisms
Earned only by Ascending — the deeper you clear first, the more you get. Spend it on the permanent Ascension Tree.
Comets
Earned from Deeds, Daily Quests and login streaks. Exclusive unlocks: Auto-Ascend, Comet Trials, Rift Trail and Starfall Crest. Auto-Ascend plus Trials unlock Quest Refresh; previous complete Rest Stop owners retain access. Trials and cosmetics grant no power or currency bonuses.
Sigils
Dropped by Rift bosses. First unlock Mythic Wisp Ultimates; after every Ultimate is owned, spend 25 to ready one Active Wisp ability, up to 3 times per Ascension run.
Core Mechanics
Push
Rift mode
Climb toward new Rifts and bosses. Your saved Push point is preserved if you switch to Farm.
Rift Regions
World progression
The Rift changes region every 25 levels, moving through the Starlit Verge, Ashen Canopy, Glass Wastes, Drowned Observatory, Void Basilica and Crown of Night before deeper echoes begin.
Farm
Rift mode
Repeat your highest cleared non-boss Rift for steady resources, then return to the exact Push point when ready.
Wisp Power
Combat stat
Level and Rarity set each Wisp’s Power. It feeds passive damage and that Wisp’s damaging or resource ability. Support buff strength is fixed by the ability and its Ultimate, not by Wisp Power.
Passive Wisp Damage
Combat rule
Active Wisp Power is multiplied by passive-only permanent upgrades, applicable damage Bonds and active Support buffs. Modules and Ultimates do not increase passive damage.
Ability Output
Combat / economy rule
Damaging abilities use Wisp Power, their relevant Module, Ultimate, damage Bonds and Boss ability modifiers. Gale/Thorn resource output uses Wisp Power, its Module, Ultimate and Dawnpriest; passive-only party upgrades and Support buffs do not increase ability output.
Tap damage (Guardian Tap)
Damage from tapping the enemy
This is your damage per tap on the enemy. Tap starts at 5 damage plus 2% of your general Active-Wisp passive power, then Tap upgrades apply. Support buffs and Guardian’s Mark also multiply it. Auto-Tap uses the same hit once per second.
Rarity
Wisp progression
Rarity multiplies that Wisp’s Power, so it affects passive damage plus damaging/resource abilities. Every Rarity tier owned across the roster also adds +2% general passive-party power. Rarity does not strengthen Support buffs.
Modules & Ultimates
Wisp progression
Modules are role-specific: Burst/Breaker Modules boost ability damage, Shard/Lumen Utility Modules boost their ability-generated resource, and Amplifier Modules boost Motes while Active. Ultimates double damage/resource ability output; Amplifier Ultimates change the buff from +25% for 4s to +50% for 8s.
Endgame Currency Utility
Economy rule
After all eight Ultimates are owned, Sigils can ready one Active Wisp ability for 25 Sigils, at most 3 times per Ascension run. Auto-Ascend plus Comet Trials unlock Quest Refresh; previous complete Rest Stop owners retain access. A refresh costs at least the richest quest reward, so refreshing cannot generate extra Comets.
Wisp Roles
Build label
Roles describe authoritative ability output: Burst delivers the highest raw ability coefficient; Breaker delivers heavy ability hits; Amplifier buffs passive Wisp damage and your tap damage; Shard Utility and Lumen Utility add their named resource to ability casts. These are output and utility roles, not defensive combat roles.
Ascend
Permanent progression
After clearing at least 15 Rifts, restart the run for Prisms. Your first reward sets a cleared-Rift benchmark; repeats at or below it earn a 20% reserve reward, while pushing beyond it adds a new-depth bonus. Permanent systems stay.
Luminous Enemies
Rare encounter
Rare non-boss enemies that drop Motes. Their appearance chance rises as you push deeper.
Boss Traits
Boss mechanic
Regrowth regenerates 0.9% max HP/s. Fractured Core regenerates 0.5%/s and takes +75% from Wisp ability hits only. Guardian’s Mark regenerates 0.6%/s and makes your manual taps and Auto-Tap deal x3; passive Wisp damage is unchanged by those trait bonuses.
Offline Progress
Idle system
Combat, Wisp abilities, Auto-Tap, Farm, Auto-Ascend, Long Studies and automation continue while you are away. If Auto-Empower makes you strong enough after a boss retreat, the game retries the saved Boss automatically.
